about: Newer editions of the numbers the talk uses

figures.talk_figure: $17.4M average annual cost of insider risk (2025 report)
figures.newer_figure: $19.5M average annual cost (2026 report, data for 2025), up 20% over two years; negligence $10.3M; 67 days to contain
figures.quote: The average annual cost of insider risk reached $19.5 million in 2025, up 20% over two years, while the average time to contain an incident fell to a record low.
figures.recommendation: Update to $19.5M, cite '2026 Cost of Insider Risks Global Report, Ponemon/DTEX' (354 organisations, 8,750 interviews). Negligence at $10.3M (+17%) suits 'not attacks, just agents being agents'. Grade A2 (one sponsor-commissioned survey, checked capture).

figures.newer_figure: 109:1 (2026 Identity Security Landscape, now published by Palo Alto Networks after the CyberArk acquisition; n=2,930)
figures.quote: Organizations are currently contending with an average of 109 machine identities for every human. AI agents are the fastest-growing subset of that population.
figures.recommendation: Update to 109:1 and attribute to 'Palo Alto Networks (formerly CyberArk) 2026 Identity Security Landscape'. Same page: 96% say human identities have access far beyond their roles. Vendor survey, A2.

figures.newer_figure: Human element 62% (from 60%); third-party involvement 48% of breaches (up 60% from 30%)
figures.quote: Human element was present in 62% of breaches, a slight increase from the previous year’s 60%. ... breaches with third-party involvement have increased by 60% from last year’s dataset, reaching 48% of total breaches.
figures.recommendation: Update both. 48% third party is a big jump and strengthens the 'delegated access' beat (Drift, Vercel/Context.ai are 2025-26 examples). Careful: ransomware is also 48% of breaches in the same report; do not confuse. Primary PDF captured, A6 for the figure as Verizon's.

figures.talk_figure: Over 40% of agentic AI projects canceled by end of 2027 (Gartner, 25 June 2025)
figures.newer_figure: No revision of the 40% cancellation forecast found. New: by 2027, 40% of enterprises will demote or decommission autonomous AI agents due to governance gaps identified only after production incidents (26 May 2026). Also: 70% of enterprises will abandon agentic AI built by vendor forward-deployed engineering by 2028 (29 Sept 2026).
figures.quote: Gartner predicts that by 2027, 40% of enterprises will demote or decommission autonomous AI agents due to governance gaps identified only after production incidents occur.
figures.recommendation: Keep the 2025 figure (still current) and add the May 2026 one: it ties cancellations to production incidents, which is exactly the talk's argument. gartner.com returns 403; captured from Gartner's own gcom.pdo.aws.gartner.com mirror plus a republication. It is a prediction: label 'guess', not measured.

figures.newer_figure: 73% expect agents to become vital within a year; 68% cannot clearly distinguish human from AI agent activity (CSA, March 2026)
figures.quote: Seventy-three percent of organizations expect AI agents to become vital within the next year, yet 68% can’t clearly distinguish between human and AI agent activity
figures.recommendation: Good for 'your logs are a self-report' / attribution beat. Survey, A2.

figures.newer_figure: 33% of developers using agents say their company had an incident tied to overprivileged NHIs; 40% grant persistent access; agents at 41% of orgs reach more than approved (1Password, n=1,000, fielded 26 May to 3 June 2026)
figures.quote: Among developers who use agents, 33% said their company had a breach or security incident tied to overprivileged non-human identities.
figures.recommendation: Promising but captured only through a vendor blog summarising 1Password's survey (A1). Fetch 1Password's own release before using.

figures.newer_figure: Reported Gartner Market Guide for Guardian Agents (25 Feb 2026) claim that through 2028 at least 80% of unauthorised AI agent transactions will be caused by internal policy violations rather than malicious attacks
figures.quote: On February 25, 2026, Gartner published its inaugural Market Guide for Guardian Agents
figures.recommendation: Would be the perfect support for 'not attacks, just agents being agents', but the 80% wording was only seen in a vendor press release that returned 403; the captured THN piece confirms the guide exists, not the 80% figure. A1 until captured.
